Radiative Transfer

Disc temperatures in cuDisc are computed self-consistently by solving the frequency-dependent radiative transfer problem in 2D. The method combines ray-tracing for the direct stellar irradiation with a flux-limited diffusion (FLD) approximation for thermal re-emission and scattering.

The hybrid approach

Computing the full frequency-resolved radiative transfer problem in 2D on every time step is computationally prohibitive. cuDisc therefore splits the radiation field into two components:

  1. Direct stellar irradiation is computed with frequency-resolved ray-tracing. This gives an exact treatment of the direct stellar heating and single-scattered light.

  2. Thermal re-emission (dust thermal emission and the diffuse radiation field) is computed with a multifrequency FLD solver. FLD is a computationally efficient approximation to the full radiative transfer equation that works well in both optically thick (diffusion) and optically thin (free-streaming) limits.

Energy equations

The internal energy of the gas-dust mixture and the radiation field are coupled through the equations (Robinson et al. 2024, Eqs. 39–40):

\[\begin{split}\frac{\partial (\rho C_v T)}{\partial t} &= -\nabla\cdot\mathbf{F}_\text{diff} + \sum_\nu \rho\kappa_\nu^P \bigl(4\pi B_\nu - c E_\nu\bigr) + \Gamma_\text{visc}, \\[4pt] \frac{\partial E_\nu}{\partial t} &= \nabla\cdot\!\left(\frac{c}{3\rho\kappa_\nu}\nabla E_\nu\right) - \rho\kappa_\nu^P \bigl(c E_\nu - 4\pi B_\nu\bigr) + S_\nu^\text{star},\end{split}\]

where Eν = cJν is the frequency-specific radiation energy density (proportional to the mean intensity Jν), Bν is the Planck function, κνP is the Planck-mean opacity, and Γ:sub:visc is the viscous heating rate.

Flux-limited diffusion

The FLD approximation replaces the exact radiative flux with

\[\mathbf{F}_\nu = -\frac{c\,\lambda_\nu}{\rho\kappa_\nu}\,\nabla E_\nu,\]

where λν is the flux limiter. cuDisc uses the Kley (1989) limiter (Eqs. 42–43), which interpolates between the diffusion regime (λ = 1/3) and the free-streaming regime (λ → c |∇E| / E):

\[\lambda_\nu = \frac{1}{R_\nu}\!\left(\coth R_\nu - \frac{1}{R_\nu}\right), \quad R_\nu = \frac{|\nabla E_\nu|}{\rho\kappa_\nu E_\nu}.\]

Multifrequency treatment

The FLD equation is solved on n_bands frequency bands rather than a single grey opacity. Each band has its own opacity and radiation energy density, and the bands are coupled through the Planck source term \(\rho\kappa_\nu^P(cE_\nu - 4\pi B_\nu)\). The Planck-weighted opacity in each band is recomputed at each temperature update to account for the temperature-dependent dust emission spectrum.

Stellar irradiation

The stellar heating rate Sstar is computed by ray-tracing radially outward from the star (Eq. 45). For each frequency bin in the stellar spectrum, a ray is cast from the star, and the optical depth along the ray is accumulated. The absorbed power per unit volume at each cell is

\[S_\nu^\text{star} = \rho\kappa_\nu^P\,F_\nu^\star\, e^{-\tau_\nu},\]

where Fν★ is the stellar flux and τν is the optical depth from the star to the cell.

Scattered light is handled by computing the first-order scattering source:

\[S_\nu^\text{sca} = \rho\kappa_\nu^\text{sca}\,F_\nu^\star\, e^{-\tau_\nu^\text{ext}},\]

where κνsca is the scattering opacity and τνext is the optical depth to extinction. This single-scattering source is then passed to the FLD solver as an additional heating term.

Viscous heating

Turbulent viscous dissipation heats the gas at a rate

\[\Gamma_\text{visc} = \frac{9}{4}\,\nu\,\Omega_K^2\,\rho_g,\]

where ΩK is the Keplerian angular velocity. This is added to the right-hand side of the internal energy equation at each cell.

Opacities

cuDisc uses frequency-resolved dust opacities from the DSHARP opacity table (Birnstiel et al. 2018), which provides absorption and scattering cross-sections as a function of grain size and wavelength. The total opacity field is computed from the sum over all grain-size bins and the gas contribution:

\[\rho\kappa_\nu = \sum_k \rho_{d,k}\,\kappa_{\nu,k}^\text{abs} + \rho_g\,\kappa_{\nu,g},\]

where the gas opacity κν,g is set to a fixed small floor (set_k_g_min_grain).

Temperature convergence

At the start of a simulation, and whenever the dust distribution changes significantly, the temperature must be iterated to self-consistency. A typical iteration updates the opacities, re-solves the FLD equation, and then re-solves the hydrostatic equilibrium until the fractional change in temperature falls below 10-5.

Benchmarks

The temperature solver has been validated against the Pinte et al. (2009) benchmark, which provides a reference temperature structure computed with a full Monte Carlo radiative transfer code for a flared disc with a single grain size. The cuDisc FLD result agrees with the reference to within a few percent over most of the disc. Details of this benchmark are given in Tests.
